raw_response:
Aiya, you want to know how I'll manage my land this year? Let me think it through.

I'm getting old — 75 now, these hands aren't what they were. My wife helps when she can but she's not young either. Just the two of us on 5 mu. Small piece of land, but it's ours, and we've been doing wheat and maize on it as long as I can remember. My father did the same. Everyone in the village does wheat-maize. No reason to change now.

**Wheat first, because that's what's in the ground soon enough — actually it went in last October.**

I planted the wheat back in early October, same time as always. Used seed I got from the agricultural supply shop in town — Jimai variety, the one the shop owner recommended last year and it did alright. About 15 yuan per jin for seed, maybe 15-18 jin per mu. I don't save wheat seed anymore, the new varieties do better and everyone says old saved seed gets weak after a few years.

For fertilizer on wheat, I put down compound fertilizer before planting — one bag (50 jin) covers about 1.5 mu, that's my base. Then in spring when the wheat turns green and starts jointing, I topdress with urea. Maybe 15 jin of urea per mu at that time. My neighbor Lao Wang uses more, says the extension people told him to, but fertilizer is expensive and my land has been farmed a long time, it's not bad soil. I stick with what works.

Irrigation for wheat — I need to water it. We have the well, but pumping costs money, electricity isn't free. I'll water it: once before winter (dong shui, that's important, the old people always said so), once at green-up in March, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if it doesn't rain. So three, maybe four times. If it rains good in spring I skip one.

Pesticide — I spray once for weeds in spring, 2,4-D type, cheap. If I see aphids at heading I'll spray once more. Nothing fancy.

Harvest is early June. I don't have a combine — I hire the combine guy who comes through the village. About 60 yuan per mu. My wife and I can't cut 5 mu by hand anymore, those days are gone.

**Then maize, right after wheat comes off.**

Very tight turnaround, maybe 5-7 days between wheat harvest and maize planting. No time for plowing — I do no-till, plant the maize right into the wheat stubble with the hired seeder. That's how everyone does it now. Plant mid-June.

Maize seed has to be hybrid, you can't save it — I buy from the shop, Zhengdan or whatever they have, maybe 25-30 yuan per mu for seed. I use about 4-5 jin per mu.

Fertilizer for maize — I put compound fertilizer down at planting through the seeder, then when the maize is waist-high (big trumpet stage, da la ba kou) I topdress urea, maybe 15-20 jin per mu. That's the important one, my father taught me that, "zhuang tou bu zhuang wei" — feed the head not the tail.

Maize irrigation — usually 1 or 2 times. If July-August rains are good, maybe none. If it's dry at tasseling I MUST water, that's when water matters most. Skip water at tasseling and you lose everything.

Pesticide on maize — spray once for corn borer when I see the damage on leaves. Nothing else usually.

Harvest late September, hire the combine again, about 70 yuan per mu. Sell some, keep some for the family and for feed.

**About money and labor** — I'm watching every yuan. Pension is small. Son works in town, sends a little but not much. I can't afford to gamble on expensive inputs. Stick with what works. If I have a bad year, 5 mu is all I have — no cushion.

Expected yield? Wheat maybe 400 jin per mu if weather is normal — that's 400 kg, we count in jin mostly but I know the kg too. Maize maybe 450 kg per mu. Good years a bit more, bad years less. Last year was okay, nothing special.
